title: FAC-06 S0: foundation hubs (migration 6, protocol fields, route stubs, events, config keys, UI route placeholders)
body:
## Goal
Land every shared/hub change for FAC-06 Scope A in one slice so later slices only add new files or fill stubs.

## Contract
1. Migration 6 in internal/controlplane/store.go (current schema is user_version=5; continue the hand-rolled sequence, additive only, a v5 DB must upgrade in place without data loss):
   - `job_labels(job_id TEXT, label_key TEXT, value TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(job_id,label_key))` + index on `(label_key,value)`
   - `jobs.supersedes_job_id` (nullable)
   - `runs.failure_class`, `runs.reset_at`, `runs.reset_source`, `runs.incarnation` (nullable)
   - `workers.incarnation` (INTEGER default 0)
   - `executor_state(worker, executor, unavailable_until, backoff_seconds, reset_source, updated_at, PRIMARY KEY(worker,executor))`
   - `run_usage(run_id PRIMARY KEY, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, reasoning_tokens, created_at)`
   - `events(id, type, subject_kind, subject_id, cause, payload_json, created_at)` + index on `(type, created_at)`
   - `run_log_tail(run_id PRIMARY KEY, next_offset INTEGER, data BLOB, truncated INTEGER, updated_at)`
   Fresh databases end at user_version=6.
2. internal/controlplane/events.go: `type Event struct{Type, SubjectKind, SubjectID, Cause string; Payload any; CreatedAt time.Time}` and `AppendEvent(ctx, tx *sql.Tx, e Event) error` (store method) that inserts a row (payload marshalled to JSON) and mirrors it to slog. Event types used later: rate_limit_stall_start, rate_limit_stall_end, auth_change, cancel, usage.
3. internal/protocol/protocol.go, all `omitempty`: `Completion{FailureClass string; ResetAt *time.Time; ResetSource string; Usage *Usage}`; `type Usage struct{Model string; InputTokens, OutputTokens, CachedInputTokens, ReasoningTokens int64}` (json snake_case); `PollRequest.Incarnation int64` (InstanceID already exists); `RunSpec.Incarnation int64` (RunSpec is the lease); `type LogChunk struct{Offset int64; Data []byte; Truncated bool}` (json offset/data/truncated).
4. server.go `submitRequest` gains `Labels map[string]string "labels,omitempty"` and `SupersedesJobID string "supersedes_job_id,omitempty"` (decoded but ignored until T12).
5. internal/config/config.go `Server` gains `RetentionDays *int toml:"retention_days"` (default 90) and `FinishedLimit *int toml:"finished_limit"` (default 50) with accessor methods; add commented `# retention_days = 90` / `# finished_limit = 50` lines under `[server]` in examples/config.toml. (The CP's section is `[server]`; `[control_plane]` is worker-side.)
6. New internal/controlplane/routes_fac06.go: `func (s *Server) registerFAC06Routes(mux *http.ServeMux)`, called from the route table in server.go. Routes and the per-feature stub file that holds each handler (each stub writes 501 via a shared `notImplemented(w)` helper):
   - GET /api/v1/jobs -> listJobs, GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} -> authorizeArtifact(jobDetail), GET /api/v1/runs/{id} -> authorizeArtifact(runDetail), GET /api/v1/events -> listEvents   [read_api.go]
   - POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel -> authorizeSubmission(cancelJob)   [cancel.go]  (literal segment wins over existing /jobs/{id}/{action})
   - POST /api/v1/executors/{worker}/{executor}/clear-rate-limit -> authorizeSubmission(clearRateLimit)   [executors_http.go]
   - POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/log -> authorizeWorker(appendRunLog), GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/log -> authorizeArtifact(runLog)   [runlog.go]
   - GET /api/v1/usage -> usageRollup   [usage_http.go]
   - POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/rewind -> authorizeSubmission(rewindJob)   [rewind.go]
7. UI hash routes in src/routes.js (keep existing `#/runs/<jobID>` = job/task detail unchanged): `#/run/<runID>` -> {view:"run", runID}, `#/gate/<jobID>` -> {view:"gate", jobID}, `#/usage` -> {view:"usage"}. main.jsx renders placeholder components exported from new files src/run-detail.jsx (RunDetail), src/gate-panel.jsx (GatePanel), src/usage.jsx (UsagePage) and adds a Usage nav entry. Extend routes.test.js.
Tests in internal/controlplane/migration6_test.go: TestMigration6FreshDB (user_version=6, all tables/columns exist), TestMigration6UpgradesV5 (a v5 DB with a job+run upgrades, rows intact), TestMigration6RouteStubs (each new route answers 501 when authorized), TestAppendEvent.

title: FAC-06 S1: side-effect-free GET /status + retention pruning (D7, D27)
body:
## Goal
GET handlers must only read. Move maintenance out of GET /api/v1/status and add retention pruning to the background scheduler.

## Contract
- Remove the `s.maintainState` call from `(*Server).status` in server.go (the scheduler loop at server.go ~L247 `loop(true, s.maintainState)` already runs it). This one-line deletion is the only server.go edit.

Register it in the same scheduler loop (inside retention.go via a hook the loop calls, or one added line next to maintainState).

title: FAC-06 S2: slim list/detail read API + /status v-schema (D8, D10, D25, D15)
body:
## Goal
Slim /status and add list/detail endpoints so list bodies never carry prompt/spec text, and publish the stable /status v-schema that Scope B codes against.

## Contract
Fill the stubs in read_api.go (created by T0) and add the schema structs.
- GET /api/v1/status returns:
```
{ schema_version: 1, generated_at: RFC3339,
  jobs: [slim job summary],            // no prompt, spec or rendered text; finished jobs capped at [server] finished_limit (default 50), active jobs never capped
  connections: [...unchanged...],
  executors: [], gates_awaiting_approval: [], blocked_jobs: [], logins: [],
  ...all other existing top-level fields unchanged }
executors item = {id, worker, executor, state:"ok"|"rate_limited", since, reason, message, rate_limited_until: RFC3339|null, reset_source:"structured"|"regex"|"estimate"|null}
Item = {id, state, since: RFC3339, reason (CamelCase), message, html_url}
```
  The four arrays are always present (never null) and empty in this slice; T11 fills executors[], T14 fills the Item arrays. Put the Go structs in status_schema.go and the slim summary builder in job_summary.go.
- GET /api/v1/jobs?state=&label=k:v&limit= -> {jobs:[slim summary]} (label filter joins job_labels).
- GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} -> job detail (spec/prompt allowed) + at most 20 most recent runs; 404 unknown. Behind authorizeArtifact.
- GET /api/v1/runs/{id} -> run detail incl. result, events, rendered_prompt; 404 unknown. Behind authorizeArtifact.
- Contract for Scope B: every run object in /jobs/{id} runs[] and the /runs/{id} body ALWAYS has keys `failure_class` (string|null), `reset_at` (RFC3339|null), `reset_source` ("structured"|"regex"|"estimate"|null), read from the migration-6 columns (null until T10 writes them).
- GET /api/v1/events?type=&since=RFC3339&limit= -> {events:[{id,type,subject_kind,subject_id,cause,payload,created_at}]} newest first.
- Update existing UI code only if needed to compile; the UI switches to these APIs in T3.
Tests (read_api_test.go): TestStatusSlim (no prompt/spec substrings in /status or /jobs bodies; finished cap), TestStatusSchemaGolden (golden JSON under testdata asserting every v-schema key and the null failure_class/reset_at/reset_source keys; hand-rolled -update flag), TestJobDetail, TestRunDetail, TestDetailAuth (cross-origin GET without token -> 403; worker token -> 200), TestEventsAPI.

title: FAC-06 S3: visibility-aware usePolling + UI on the slim API (D17)
body:
## Goal
Make the UI poll through one visibility-aware hook and load job detail from the new detail endpoint instead of /status.

## Contract
- New src/use-polling.js: `usePolling(fetcher, intervalMs) -> {data, error, refresh}`. Polls every intervalMs while `document.visibilityState === "visible"`; pauses entirely while hidden; fetches immediately once when the tab becomes visible again; `refresh()` forces a fetch; cleans up timers/listeners on unmount. Export a framework-free core (e.g. `createPoller`) so it is testable with node:test mock.timers. No new npm dependencies.
- status-loader.js is wrapped by usePolling (main.jsx uses it; later slices read new /status fields and do not edit the loader).
- task-detail.jsx loads `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` when opened (prompt/spec now come from there, not /status) and shows runs from its runs[].
- connections.jsx: replace both setInterval usages with usePolling.
- Tests: src/use-polling.test.js (mock.timers: 0 fetches while hidden across several intervals, exactly 1 on becoming visible, interval resumes); keep status-ui.test.js and connections.test.js green (update fixtures for the slim schema).

title: FAC-06 S4: cancel semantics (D9)
body:
## Goal
Give job cancellation precise, idempotent HTTP semantics and make workers treat 404/409 as terminal.

## Contract
- Implement `cancelJob` in internal/controlplane/cancel.go (stub from T0) for POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel: 202 if the job was active and is now cancelling/cancelled; 200 if already cancelled (idempotent); 409 if finished in any other state; 404 unknown. Body: `{job_id, state}`.
- Direct (non-workflow) jobs go through a new `store.CancelDirectJob(ctx, id)`; workflow jobs keep using the existing WorkflowAction path.
- Append a `cancel` event (AppendEvent from T0) in the same tx.
- Export a helper usable inside another tx, e.g. `cancelJobTx(ctx, tx, id) (status int, err error)`, because T12 (supersede) reuses it.
- internal/managedworker/worker.go: response handling only — a 404 or 409 from heartbeat or cancel-related calls stops the run cleanly (process killed, no retry loop, no failed completion spam).
- Tests: cancel_test.go TestCancel* (all four codes, direct and workflow jobs, event appended); worker_test.go TestWorkerTerminalOn404 (fake CP returns 404 then 409 on heartbeat -> run stops, no further heartbeats).

## Files owned
- internal/controlplane/cancel.go
- internal/controlplane/cancel_test.go
- internal/managedworker/worker.go
- internal/managedworker/worker_test.go

## Acceptance

title: FAC-06 S5: stable worker instance ID + incarnation (D6)
body:
## Goal
Workers get a persistent identity; a restarted worker process interrupts its own orphaned runs.

## Contract
- internal/managedworker/identity.go: `LoadOrCreateInstanceID(stateDir string) (string, error)` — UUIDv4 persisted at `<worker state dir>/instance_id` (0600, created atomically); reused on restart. The worker's existing `instanceID` field and PollRequest.InstanceID use it. Also track a per-process incarnation value the worker sends in `PollRequest.Incarnation` (0 = unknown, CP assigns).
- internal/controlplane/incarnation.go: on the first poll from a (worker name, instance_id) whose process is new, bump `workers.incarnation`; stamp `runs.incarnation` when leasing (and set `RunSpec.Incarnation`); in the SAME transaction mark runs of that worker with an older incarnation still in `running` state as `interrupted`. Minimal hook call(s) in the existing poll/lease code are allowed.
- Tests: identity_test.go TestInstanceIDPersists (same ID across two loads, new ID in a fresh dir); incarnation_test.go TestIncarnationInterrupts (lease a run, simulate restart poll, old run becomes interrupted, new lease gets higher incarnation).

## Files owned

title: FAC-06 S6: per-entry config validation + `machinist config validate` (D20)
body:
## Goal
One bad command entry must not take down the control plane, and operators get a validator CLI.

## Contract
- internal/config/validate.go: two-phase load. Phase 1 parses the TOML file; a syntax error returns an error and the running CP keeps its last good config. Phase 2 decodes/validates each `[commands.*]` (and workflow) entry separately; a bad entry becomes `InvalidCommand{Name string; Reason string}` with Reason formatted `file:line:col: message` (go-toml positions) and is excluded from the loaded config. Expose `ValidateFile(path) (Report, error)`.
- /api/v1/status gains top-level `invalid_commands: [{name, reason}]` (always present, [] when none). Minimal wiring in the CP config load/status path is allowed.
- internal/cli/config_cmd.go: `machinist config validate [--config PATH] [--json]`; human output lists problems; --json prints `{valid: bool, invalid_commands:[{name,reason}], error: string|null}`; exit 0 when valid, 1 on any error. Register the `config` group with ONE line in internal/cli/root.go.
- Tests: validate_test.go TestPerEntryValidation (one good + one bad entry -> good loads, bad reported with file:line:col; syntax error -> error); config_cmd_test.go TestConfigValidateCmd (exit codes, --json shape).

## Files owned

title: FAC-06 S7: login hysteresis state machine (D5)
body:
## Goal
Stop a single flaky auth check from marking an executor login expired.

## Contract
- internal/controlplane/auth_hysteresis.go: `type authFSM struct{...}`; `Observe(result CheckResult, now time.Time) (state string, recheckAt time.Time)`. States: `ok`, `rechecking`, `expired`. Rules: first soft failure from ok -> `rechecking` with a fast recheck (e.g. now+30s); a second consecutive soft failure -> `expired`; any success -> `ok` and resets the counter; a past `expires_at` or an explicit 401/logout -> `expired` immediately. Clock and checker injected.
- Wire it at the existing auth-state update call site in auth_store.go; on every state change append an `auth_change` event (subject = worker/executor, payload {from,to}).
- Tests: auth_hysteresis_test.go TestAuthHysteresis (table-driven, testing/synctest), covering each rule and the event.

## Files owned
- internal/controlplane/auth_hysteresis.go
- internal/controlplane/auth_hysteresis_test.go
- internal/controlplane/auth_store.go

## Acceptance

title: FAC-06 S8: capped line reader + shape-based usage detection (D1, D2)
body:
## Goal
Never lose the output stream on a long line, and detect token usage from the JSON event shape instead of argv.

## Contract
- internal/runner/linereader.go: `LineReader(r io.Reader, maxLine int)` built on bufio.Reader (NOT bufio.Scanner); default maxLine 1 MiB; yields each line plus a `Truncated bool` when a line exceeded the cap (the rest of that line is discarded, reading continues).
- internal/runner/usage_shape.go: `Detect(line []byte) (protocol.Usage, bool)` picks a parser by JSON event shape: claude `{"type":"result",...usage}` / `message_delta` usage, codex `turn.completed` usage. Argv (e.g. `agent-run --contract` wrappers) is only a hint. Refactor codex_usage.go's structuredUsageCollector to use LineReader+Detect; contract/revision injection behaviour must not change.
- Golden fixtures: internal/runner/testdata/streams/*.jsonl with expected usage, hand-rolled `-update` flag. Include a claude stream, a codex stream, an `agent-run --contract` wrapped stream, and a stream containing a >64 KiB line.
- Worker sends `Completion.Usage`; CP: internal/controlplane/usage_store.go writes one `run_usage` row on complete (and a `usage` event).
- Tests: TestLineReader, TestUsageShape (runner); TestRunUsageWritten (controlplane).

title: FAC-06 S10: rate-limit store, lease skip, infra requeue (D4, D15)
body:
## Goal
A rate-limited completion parks the executor until reset and requeues the job without burning an attempt.

## Contract
- internal/controlplane/ratelimit_store.go: in `complete`, when `Completion.FailureClass=="rate_limited"`, in ONE `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` tx: write runs.failure_class/reset_at/reset_source; upsert executor_state(worker, executor) with unavailable_until=ResetAt (or now+backoff), backoff_seconds, reset_source, updated_at; requeue the job as an infrastructure retry (does NOT count against the attempt budget); AppendEvent `rate_limit_stall_start` (subject executor, payload {worker, executor, until, source}).
- Lease query skips executors whose `unavailable_until > now` for that worker; the first successful lease on an executor after expiry clears the row's unavailable_until and appends `rate_limit_stall_end` (cause `expired`).
- Also persist failure_class/reset_at/reset_source for any completion that carries them (so T2's run fields are non-null).
- Minimal hook calls in the existing complete/lease code paths are allowed.
- Tests (fake completions, synctest clock): TestRateLimitRequeue (attempt count unchanged, job queued again, event, run columns set), TestLeaseSkipsLimitedExecutor (no lease before reset, lease after, stall_end event once).

## Files owned
- internal/controlplane/ratelimit_store.go

- internal/controlplane/server.go

title: FAC-06 S16: live log backend (D16)
body:
## Goal
Ship a bounded live log tail from worker to control plane over its own endpoint, separate from heartbeats.

## Contract
- internal/runner/logring.go: bounded ring buffer of recent output (fed from the T8 LineReader path) that tracks a monotonically increasing byte offset; `Since(offset) (chunk []byte, next int64, truncated bool)`.
- internal/managedworker/logship.go: while a run is active, periodically POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/log with body protocol.LogChunk{Offset, Data, Truncated} (≤16 KiB per request; if more is pending, drop the excess and set Truncated). Independent goroutine, never blocks or delays heartbeats; failures are logged and retried next tick; stops at completion.
- internal/controlplane/runlog.go (stubs from T0): appendRunLog (authorizeWorker, lease token checked as for heartbeat) appends to run_log_tail keeping only the last 256 KiB, ignoring chunks whose offset < stored next_offset (idempotent), 204 on success; runLog (authorizeArtifact) GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/log?offset=N -> `{offset, next_offset, data (string), truncated, done}` where done=true once the run is finished.
- Tests: TestLogRing, TestLogShip (fake CP; 16 KiB cap; heartbeat not delayed), TestRunLogOffsets (duplicate offset ignored, 256 KiB cap, done flag, auth).

## Goal
Let a workflow step loop back to an earlier step when blocked, a bounded number of times.

## Contract
- internal/config/on_blocked.go: workflow step TOML field `on_blocked = { goto = "<step>", max = N }` (N ≥ 1); validation: goto must name an earlier step of the same workflow, max required; errors reported like other workflow validation errors. Add the field to the step struct in internal/config/workflows.go.
- internal/controlplane/on_blocked.go: when a step completes blocked and has on_blocked, inside the insert tx read/increment `workflow_loop_counters(job_id, edge="<from>-><goto>")`; if count < max, append a new attempt with reason `loop` (reusing T19's rewind append) targeting goto; at max the job stays blocked (normal blocked behaviour, visible in /status blocked_jobs).
- Tests: TestOnBlockedGoto (config parse/validation + a blocked step loops back and the counter increments), TestOnBlockedMax (after max loops the job stays blocked).

## Files owned
- internal/config/on_blocked.go
- internal/config/on_blocked_test.go
- internal/config/workflows.go
- internal/controlplane/on_blocked.go
- internal/controlplane/on_blocked_test.go
- internal/controlplane/workflows.go

## Acceptance
- `go test -race ./internal/config ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestOnBlockedGoto|TestOnBlockedMax'` -> PASS
- `just check` -> exit 0

Context: repo seanGSISG/machinist (Go 1.26 control plane + managed worker, React/Vite UI in internal/controlplane/web, hash routing in src/routes.js). This is FAC-06 Scope A; design decisions D1-D27 are in the approved design.md, slices S0-S20 in structure.md. Rules: new Go code goes in new per-feature files; shared structs only gain optional `omitempty` fields; schema changes are hand-rolled `PRAGMA user_version` migrations in internal/controlplane/store.go; tests are offline (httptest, testing/synctest for time, golden fixtures with a hand-rolled -update flag, UI tests on `node --test` + jsdom + mock.timers). All tests must pass under -race and `just check` must pass before merge. Do not edit files outside `owns` except to fix compile errors caused by your change.
